applicableAreas: Southeast corner of site, southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Three trees (2 Live Oak, 1 Cedar Elm) are shown on the landscape plan within 10-15 lateral feet of the existing overhead electric (OHE) line at the southern property boundary. The plant schedule identifies these species by common and scientific name but does not verify utility-compatible (UC) designation per ECM Appendix F. Trees within 15 feet of distribution conductors must be utility-compatible species. No written approval from Austin Energy is shown in the plans or supplementary documents authorizing non-compatible species in this restricted zone.

applicableAreas: Southeast corner of site, southern property boundary within 25 feet of overhead electric line
findings.comment: Three trees (Live Oak and Cedar Elm) are proposed within 25 feet of the overhead electric distribution line. The plant schedule specifies only installation height requirements (16' minimum) and does not provide mature heights necessary to determine whether these trees qualify as 'large trees' (mature height ≥40 feet per ECM Appendix F). Large trees must be at least 25 feet from distribution conductors. Without mature height verification on the plans, compliance cannot be confirmed.

applicableAreas: Southeast corner of site, along OHE line at southern property boundary
findings.comment: Utility poles are shown along the overhead electric line at the southern boundary, and three trees are positioned within the approximate area (10-15 feet from the OHE line). However, the landscape plan does not dimension specific distances from tree trunk centers to individual utility pole locations. Precise measurement would be required to verify the 10-foot minimum clearance requirement is met for all poles.

applicableAreas: Throughout site where underground electric distribution is proposed
findings.comment: Proposed underground electric lines and pull boxes are shown on the electrical plan, and trees are shown on the landscape plan, but the relationship between specific trees and specific underground equipment locations is not clearly mapped. Without precise dimensioning or clear correlation between tree locations and pull box/underground equipment locations, it cannot be verified whether any trees are within the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement.

applicableAreas: Throughout site where underground electric equipment is present
findings.comment: Trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment must include root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment). The landscape plan does not show root barrier details or specifications, and the relationship between proposed trees and underground equipment locations is not clearly documented. Cannot verify whether root barriers are required or provided.

applicableAreas: Southeast corner of site and throughout landscape plan where large trees may be proposed
findings.comment: The landscape plan shows proposed trees but does not differentiate which trees are 'large trees' (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F). The plant schedule provides only installation height specifications (16' minimum), not mature heights. Large trees must maintain 25-foot clearances from distribution conductors and 50-foot clearances from transmission conductors. Without mature height notation or differentiation on the landscape plan, large tree locations cannot be verified for compliance with clearance requirements.

applicableAreas: Southeast corner of site, within 15 feet of overhead electric line at southern property boundary
findings.comment: Three trees (2 Live Oak, 1 Cedar Elm) are proposed within 15 feet of the existing overhead electric distribution line at the southern boundary. UCM § 1.10.10.4 permits exceptions to planting distance restrictions only with explicit written approval from Austin Energy. No Austin Energy approval letter, variance, or waiver is shown on the plans or in the supplementary documents. Applicant must provide documented written approval from Austin Energy to authorize tree placement within the restricted zone, or relocate trees beyond the required clearance distance.
